clue.text: Board move found US credit note

parts.note: to have found something is to have discovered it
a cheque, a note drawing on credit, is spelt check in American English

explanation.surface: Someone discovers an American cheque, as if reporting a find on a noticeboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board move' sounds like a notice pinned up, but it is chess: a discovered check is when moving one piece uncovers an attack on the king by another.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess manoeuvre played on the board, in which moving one piece exposes the enemy king to another.

clue.text: After father retires, Abramovich welcomes new or old worker

indicators.note: after tells us the father piece comes before what follows it in the answer
to retire is to go back, so the word for father is turned round

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: one who welcomes takes someone in, so the oligarch's first name holds the letter for new

parts.note: Roman Abramovich is the Russian billionaire who owned Chelsea football club

explanation.surface: A football club owner takes on a worker, new or long-serving, once his father steps down.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman Abramovich was the Russian owner of Chelsea FC, so 'Abramovich' gives his first name; 'retires' turns the father round and 'welcomes' takes in N. 'or' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron-man was an archaic term for a mechanic or labourer, someone who wore a leather apron at work.

clue.text: Nothing left in explosive crater

indicators.note: in tells us the nothing and left letters sit inside the explosive's letters

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
the round letter O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: After a blast, nothing remains in the crater it made.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a pit or cavity in the ground, the sort of gap left after a bomb falls.

clue.text: Top trophies gaining publicity before gun shot was invented

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter of the trophies word goes

parts.note: cups are trophies awarded to winners
PR, public relations, is publicity

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters of gun are rearranged

explanation.surface: First-class trophies win publicity ahead of the day the gun was invented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' removes the head of CUPS to leave UPS; 'shot' rearranges GUN to give UNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has sprung up has arisen or come into being, as a new invention does.

clue.text: Formula 1 driver just going above 100

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: just, meaning only, is but
a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: A racing driver barely goes over a hundred miles an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenson Button is a British racing driver, Formula 1 world champion in 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenson Button raced in Formula One and won its world championship, so he is an example of such a driver.

clue.text: Universal rock star raves, injects drug — love getting unconscious?

indicators.note: something that injects takes another thing inside it, so the drug goes into the rearranged star
one who raves is wild, so the letters of star are jumbled

parts.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
the id is the unconscious part of the mind in Freudian psychology

explanation.surface: A rock star at a rave shoots up and passes out in a haze of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raves' rearranges STAR to ASTR, and 'injects' places E inside to make ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroids are lumps of stone orbiting the sun out in space, so rocks of the universe.

clue.text: It's about time! Around an hour is a pain

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of the first word are read backwards

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for around, used with dates
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: An impatient grumble at someone late by an hour, which is a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'It's about time!' hides a reversal: 'about' turns the letters of It's backwards, giving STI.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sudden sharp pain in the side, often brought on by running.

clue.text: Vaguely dine out, finish and leave your tips

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of dine are put out of order

parts.note: to finish is to terminate

indicators.note: the tips of words are their first letters, taken here from the last two words

explanation.surface: A diner eats out, finishes and leaves vague instructions about the tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DINE to INDE; 'tips' takes the first letters of 'leave' and 'your', L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Done indeterminately means done without precision or fixed limits, which is doing it vaguely.

clue.text: A politician's memory? Put freely, it's makeshift

parts.note: a, meaning one, is the Roman numeral I
MP is a Member of Parliament
ROM is read-only memory in computing

indicators.note: freely tells us the letters of put are arranged loosely

explanation.surface: A politician recalls a speech, put loosely together, that was thrown together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges PUT to PTU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is improvised on the spot without preparation, which makes it a makeshift effort.

clue.text: Fabric sale! 50% off money

indicators.note: half of the word sale is taken off, leaving its front half

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A shop advertises a fabric sale with half off the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth glossy cloth woven from silk or similar threads.

clue.text: See wings of shrike in prize photograph

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces go inside the word for prize

parts.note: a cup is a prize in sport
lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: A bird photographer spots a shrike's wings in a prize-winning shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings of' takes S and E, the outer letters of 'shrike'.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a picture taken from very near its subject, so a kind of photograph.

clue.text: Support for scrabble letters

indicators.note: to scrabble is to scramble about, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rack or stand that holds the tiles in a game of Scrabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrabble' looks like the board game but is the signal to rearrange LETTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of legs and crossbar used to hold up a table top, so a support.

clue.text: Siren's fuse?

definitions.meaning: a siren is a seductive woman, a femme fatale
to fuse is to join pieces together; the verb also means to patch or cobble together

explanation.surface: A question about what lights a siren's explosive charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking two meanings: a seductress, and to piece together or patch up.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive woman who lures men is a vamp; as a verb, vamp means to patch up or join.

clue.text: Colour sports brochure covers books …

indicators.note: one thing that covers another wraps around it, so the shuffled brochure goes round the books
sports means shows off in a different form, so the letters of brochure are rearranged

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A sports brochure has pictures on its covers of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports' and 'covers' read as nouns in the surface but are both signals: the rearranged brochure (BUROCHRE) goes round the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt ochre is a deep reddish-brown pigment, a shade used by painters.

clue.text: … on doing exercise

definitions.meaning: on means operating, as a working engine is

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: books about doing exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins the clue to the one before for the surface only; this clue has two meanings of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is on is operating; a person jogging is doing exercise on foot.

clue.text: Europeans exalting escargot at first

indicators.note: to exalt is to raise up, and in a down entry raising the pieces turns them upside down

parts.note: escargot is French for a snail
first, as 1st, is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Continental diners praise snails as the best starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exalting' reads SNAILATI from the bottom up in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Italians are people from Italy, a country in Europe, so they are Europeans.

clue.text: In the year 2000, 599 entered Open University for a bit

indicators.note: In places the inner pieces within the Roman date

parts.note: 2000 in Roman numerals is MM

indicators.note: the number entered the university, so it goes inside its letters

parts.note: OU is the Open University, a British distance-learning institution
in Roman numerals D is 500 and IC is 99

explanation.surface: A story of 599 students enrolling at the Open University in 2000, for a short course.
explanation.walkthrough: IC for 99 is a loose Roman form (strictly XCIX), accepted in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity, a little amount of something.

clue.text: Coolers designed to hold a small criminal?

definitions.text: Coolers designed to hold a small criminal?

parts.words: Coolers designed to hold a small criminal?
parts.note: cooler is slang for a prison, so tiny cells with bars for a little crook; really small hotel-room fridges

explanation.surface: Pint-sized prisons built for a pint-sized crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coolers' suggests jails, and 'small criminal' hints at a mini set of prison bars; really, the clue means little refrigerators stocked with drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fridges in hotel rooms stocked with drinks are coolers, as their name splits into tiny and prison rails.

clue.text: Clerk can bake biscuit

indicators.note: baking changes the form of a mixture, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An office worker is able to bake a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bake' rearranges CLERK and CAN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A cracknel is a light crisp biscuit, often curled or puffed up in baking.

clue.text: Getting off scary giant ride takes a little bit of nerve

indicators.note: takes means holds within, so a letter is put inside the jumbled ride
a scary ride throws things about, so the letters of giant ride are rearranged
a little bit of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A frightening fairground ride needs some nerve to get on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scary' rearranges GIANT RIDE to DETRAINIG; 'takes' slips in N, the first letter of 'nerve'.
explanation.definitionFit: To detrain is to get off a train, so detraining means alighting or getting off.

clue.text: In bath, reading yarn

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone relaxing in the bath, reading a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a tale but means thread for sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread is a fine spun strand of fibre, just as yarn is.

clue.text: Point, point, point, point then led all over the place

parts.note: a compass point, north, abbreviated N
a compass point, east, abbreviated E
another compass point, east again, abbreviated E

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so the letters of led are rearranged

explanation.surface: A repetitive stammer of points, then a scattered lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Point' is the definition; the next three are compass points N, E, E. 'all over the place' rearranges LED to DLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle is a fine sharp tip or spike, a point.

clue.text: Curse and blast without ever ending

indicators.note: without means outside, so the jumbled word goes round the letter
blast means blow apart, so the letters of and are rearranged
ending picks the final letter of the word ever

explanation.surface: A furious oath: curse and blast, without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blast' rearranges AND to DAN; 'without' wraps it round R, the last letter of 'ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: Darn is a mild oath, a softened form of damn, used as a curse.

clue.text: Lead, helium and iron compounds on Earth

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium

indicators.note: to compound is to mix, so the letters of iron are combined in a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson listing lead, helium and iron compounds found on Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as the metal beside helium and iron, but it means the leading role. 'compounds' rearranges IRON to ROIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroine is the female star of a story or film, playing its leading role.

clue.text: Coverage of space alien

parts.note: a blank is an empty space, as on a form
ET is the alien from the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Media coverage of an alien arriving from outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' looks like news reporting but means a covering on a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket is a thick covering on a bed, so a form of coverage.

clue.text: Relative to visit repeatedly after hotel checkout

indicators.note: the hotel letter checks out, leaving the word

parts.note: to haunt a place is to visit it again and again
Hotel is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for H

explanation.surface: A family member keeps visiting after leaving the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family member.

clue.text: Country relocates area to middle of mountain range

indicators.note: relocates means moves to a new position, so a letter of the country shifts
the letter is shifted to the centre of the word

parts.note: China is a country in Asia

explanation.surface: A country moves a region into the heart of its mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocates' and 'to middle of' take A from the end of CHINA and put it at the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of mountains is a connected series of peaks, a range.

clue.text: "Heavy" holds back New York gangster about the throat

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the large word wraps round the reversed abbreviation

parts.note: heavy can mean big or bulky, that is large

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A New York gang heavy grabs someone round the throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy' looks like a henchman but means big; 'back' turns the city's initials round to YN, which 'holds' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngeal means relating to the larynx, the voice box in the throat.
